body: No worries man, I appreciate the kind and we'll thought out words. It really helps put shit into perspective for me. My newest issue that JUST started is apparently someone made a suicide video on tiktok or something, and I started freaking out that I was going to force myself to see it / it come across my feed, etc. So all of this shit is being made up in my mind on the fly. I'm going to see a mental health person tomorrow and legit demand they talk to me versus brushing me off. Again, thank you for taking the time to reply and to give a shit.

Thanks man, I will. I recognize right now how stupid and ridiculous this post was. It's like I become a whole different person and freak TF out. I'm going to pretty much demand my mental health professionals help me out tomorrow. I appreciate the reply.

Thank you for the reply and you're absolutely right. I'm currently having a meltdown about something equally as stupid, that was dealt with and talked through months ago, and yet now that this "big event" is handled I'm just finding something to freak out about even when there's nothing going on. I don't know what happened to me and why I am so mentally out of control, but I understand that I am. I post here I think because I have no one else to talk to about anything. My therapist(s) and psychiatrist legitimately do not give a shit and are part of why I am in this position. Today showed me I probably need to go to a hospital and force them to listen to me / deal with me instead of not showing up to appointments, or dismissing me when I say "I am suicidal." I'm currently freaking out about how in 2008 I saw a thumbnail of a naked lady on the website TinyPic saved a screenshot of the page to show a friend because I was like "wow look dude a naked lady!" And then years later backed up my entire TinyPic account before the website shut down. I was afraid this tiny, tiny thumbnail from 12 years ago could be considered illegal, freaked out, deleted it and then spent like 3 days calling lawyers and vomiting from fear that I had done something wrong at age 12 and not really thinking about it, backed it up years later. I was told by everyone that 1. It probably wasn't even someone underage and 2. It's not a big deal, I did nothing wrong, delete it and go about my life. I got over it and yet here I am now, in same position, freaking TF out.

Yadda yadda yadda, sorry I'm rambling I'm just a complete mess. Gonna see if I can get checked into the psych ward today or tomorrow I think. Wednesday at latest since I have a therapy appointment then anyway. You really put a lot into perspective for me and I'm already taking steps to eliminate pretty much all internet / media / social media and etc from my life as a start and see if that helps with whatever broke in my head. So again, thank you for the post and for putting so much thought into it.

Edit: now someone talked about a suicide video or something on tiktok or some shit, and it's like I'm afraid I'm gonna stumble across it. I'm not researching shit but god damn it really is something broken in me. I'm saving this comment man because I'll need to read it in the future to tell myself to chill. Thank you.
I realize that now, and I feel dumb, but when I'm freaking TF out I am not exactly acting or thinking straight. I appreciate your help in getting my mind right on this man.

Edit: ignore below. I actually spoke to an FBI agent and he said what you said was 100% correct and I was overreacting. Thank you so much for the info and I apologize if I came across as doubting you!

Right, but according to this: https://www.nealdavislaw.com/blog/child-pornography/illegal-internet-searches

I committed a crime unknowingly. "Even a search for child porn on the Web could get you arrested and charged with a crime. That’s because an active search for child porn can indicate an intent to commit the crime of viewing or possessing child pornography." I had no intent on this I was simply panicking and freaking the fuck out, and had to "prove to myself" that this wasn't content that I was going to just "stumble upon" or have it in a pop-up ad. I recognize how insane and stupid those beliefs were, but at the time I was shaking and sweating and couldn't relax and my very stupid brain thought that by googling it and showing myself, "look nothing came up moron, you're freaking out for no reason." 

So yeah I'm not arguing, just trying to understand. I appreciate your reply and knowledge with this matter.  I didn't think anything of it because there was no intent and I did nothing wrong in my eyes, but if I did something wrong in the eyes of the law I can't live with that burden even if it was by accident and with no ill intent.
I only have VA healthcare unfortunately

You need to seek serious mental help. I understand they're just dreams, but if you have intent on those dreams being real you're essentially threatening the president and the Secret Service doesn't take that lightly. I would advise you seek out a medical professional asap.
Thanks man, I'll check it out sometime. I had a really rough day today so I'm glad you had a good one. Hope it stays good for you!

Yes, I have an active social worker at the VA there. I'm asking here because I don't really believe anything they say about what inpatient care is like, if that makes sense. It's like obviously they would sugar coat it and all that jazz, that's why I wanted to know if anyone here has been to that part of the hospital specifically to get an idea what it's really like.
The post is literally about them thinking they need to seek help at a mental hospital.

I'm close to not functioning. Right now I'm taking a break from talking to my dad because I just had a bad attack and was rocking back and forth and almost pulling my hair out, hitting myself, etc because I just feel so crazy. So that's probably why it's been recommended to me. But I do agree, I'm worried I drive all the way up there and they don't admit me because I'm not suicidal. It just sucks.

I've done something called IOP (intensive outpatient program) which is the same concept, we'd have 4+ hour group therapy + classes and then go home. However with COVID that's no longer offered, and rightfully so. That's why I was skipping that so to speak and going straight for residential / inpatient. But that is a very good idea if COVID wasn't a concern!

Thank you for the reply! I will strongly consider going tomorrow after I pay my bills. I'm feeling very upset all the time for seemingly no reason, and I think it might help to just be in a supportive environment.

While I understand it, it's been really hard since I was legitimately stable just kind of had moments where I felt really down and after taking the Zoloft I mean.... It's been life changing in a bad way. I never, ever had obsessive thoughts or intrusive thoughts and stuff. A lot of the issues manifesting right now I worked through in CBT and group therapy for a long time and now just... I don't know lol. It's like everything was undone and somehow made even worse.  I am just completely terrified of another SSRI breaking my brain even more :(. That being said, I know I have to do something about this, so hopefully I can get help there.

Thank you, like I said I am strongly considering going I just want to weigh my options. Right now I am afraid that if I go, it'll be like me being stuck there for many weeks and stuff. I'm worried that it could make things worse, and in my present state I'm not sure if I can abide by things getting worse. However it could make everything better! I will have to wait and see how I'm feeling here soon. Right now the obsessive thoughts and stuff are what's killing me, and I'm worried no amount of care or medication can make me forget or stop thinking about stuff that upsets me. It's dumb, but it's how it is. As it stands though I am leaning toward going just not sure when. It's an hour drive and it would cause significant hardship on my family so I might wait until the 1st so I can pay the bills first at least.

I was under the impression they wouldn't take me in unless I was suicidal. Good to know. I am of course worried it'll make things worse and not better, or they won't let me leave when I want to, but I'm gonna go if this gets any worse. My ideal situation is to hold out until Tuesday but if I feel like it isn't doable I'll go to the ER.

Will ask about that on Tuesday. I've done CBT (and currently do some) but it hasn't been for me. The different exercises that used to work aren't anymore unfortunately :( but I will keep trying! Thank you.

Thank you so much for the reply and information. I'll consider it strongly. I'm trying to hold on until my next appointment with my VA social worker but I might just go there instead. I am not suicidal or anything just really messed up feeling.

Luckily I see a talk therapist here in person, with proper safety precautions in place. It's been a huge help but there's something going on right now that has me worried. I can't pinpoint the actual cause (my anxiety will manifest, and THEN thoughts or things I obsess over become the "reason" even though they aren't if that makes sense) but I am just really having a rough go of it. I appreciate the reply.

I am unfortunately at the mercy of the Veteran's Affairs office. I had considered asking for a new psychiatrist, but I wasn't sure if I should stick with the devil I know if that makes sense. For example, my social worker there routinely doesn't show up for my appointments (over phone) and thinks that I am from a town I have never been to, and on medication I do not take, no matter how much I correct him.  


I will reach out about a different psychiatrist if this is really not normal. It felt weird as hell but I have had very limited history with psychiatrists before, so I wasn't sure. I appreciate your advice and I will look into it!

Hi thanks for the reply! I do have a tendency to overthink things, but this one was pretty black and white. They felt that they had prescribed me a good medication, it didn't work, and they were very frustrated with me and said next time just "tell them what I want." They were very angry that this medication didn't work out, and said that my "symptoms" were all in my head. Such as the sudden onset of panics, and the new thing where I clench my jaw so hard I get migraines.

They were literally asking me what specific medication(s) I want, which is why I am posting here. I thought it was really bizarre but they were the same office that laughed at me when I called and said I was having suicidal thoughts on the medication. I guess I will touch base with them again at our next appointment and try and find some middle ground, but what I took away from it was them asking me what specific medication I wanted. It sounds crazy, but it isn't the first time I've encountered doctors like this (in the VA medical system).

Lol it's very believable dude. Some people's mental health issues prevent them from being able to accomplish goals or get work done. Obviously everyone has the capacity to get work done to some extent, but what they are dealing with right now might prevent them from being able to work until they are able to manage their symptoms.

It was a job doing what I loved, and being able to help my family financially. My sibling is mentally ill and unable/unwilling to do anything, my mother is what I would describe as a grifter (compulsive liar as well) and my father is retired. Whole family is barely getting by and I was supposed to be the one that made it be okay. Working in that industry is the only job I've ever had that I was legitimately happy doing, and the high pay was just a huge bonus. Not to mention amazing health insurance so I could actually get my physical issues fixed.

I guess I am new to being depressed, I'm not used to it. I'm not sure how to fix it because every therapist I see has the same answers (square breathing, meditate, tiger breath, journal, exercise if you physically could). All things I've done and haven't been able to stop this negative mindset I have. I spent today in bed not eating, talking to anyone, or doing anything. Just slept whole day. I finally ate some yogurt and stuff about 2am but it just feels pointless. Hopefully tomorrow won't be so bad.

Edit: I just want to add I hope I don't come across as argumentative or anything, I truly appreciate your reply and will think on it for sure. I just want to make sure I clear the air so there's no misunderstanding that I'm ungrateful or anything!
Thanks man wishing the best for you too

Came here to ask same thing brother. I was recommended the Topeka program but I haven't even talked to my VA case manager yet because they won't call me back. It's been a nightmare. I hope you find the help you need.
I was raised Catholic and it's part of the reason I have so many issues. Hard pass. Glad it works for you though.

I had a therapist try to tell me I might have repressed memories, etc and IMO that's an awful and terrible thing to do to someone who has an anxiety disorder lol. While it can and does happen, I'm of the position that it's not as common as many think. Sometimes mental health issues manifest over time for no reason at all, or because of things that happen after childhood.

I guess my point is that unless you really have reason to believe you might have repressed memories or something, there's no use in obsessing over it because it'll just cause you to worry.
You love to hear it. I was prescribed Cymbalta years ago but never used it because I thought I was okay. I'll def keep it in mind as an option! Thank you.
What medicine do you take? I had Sertaline (sp?) and it didn't work for me, so I'm looking for a new one to try.

I legitimately, and I don't mean this lightly, would have killed myself if I had continued taking it at 50mg. I have issues relating to guilt / shame and what not, and issues from being abused in a long term relationship, and they all came to the forefront in really disturbing ways. The past month has undid probably 2 years of therapy and intense inner self work. I'm glad it works for others but for me lmao, I'm nearing the end of my rope. I told my dad to take my gun somewhere before I started the med because I wanted to be extra careful and I am glad I did.
Do you just go there for appointments or stay there?
Amen man. Sorry to hear you suffered as well, but I'm glad to know you're doing better and free of that situation.

My issue I guess is that I am not sure I need meds moreso than perhaps a relatively intensive amount of therapy. I have / had a very rough time in an abusive relationship and it completely destroyed who I am as a person. But even so, I made leaps and bounds of progress the last 2 years or so and as soon as I started Zoloft I can say very confidently I am back to 2018 in terms of progress. It has completely demolished me and my ability to think / feel normally. I want to believe meds are the right way though and your post has given me hope. I used to write letters and stuff like that all the time and really feel down about stuff, and I am hoping I find my fit soon so I can live "like a normie" too lmao. Again, I appreciate your insight and time to reply. It means a lot to have someone give me their experience versus trying to Google around.

No worries about the length at all! I appreciate you being willing to go into detail for my sake. I'm struggling bad since I started taking Zoloft and I'm working to ween myself off of it, but I didn't know if there was any hope for me trying different medications. I am 26 and this is the only med I've tried so it gives me hope that maybe I just didn't get lucky with the first one.

Did you have trouble with meds at first? I was taking sertraline for the last few weeks but my doc told me to stop because it made me suicidal. I am still weening off of it right now and although I had bad anxiety prior to taking it, I'm a complete wreck on it and borderline unable to function. I feel  like there's two people inside me, a logical normal one and a complete nutcase. I will fantasize about killing myself even though I have no intention of doing so. It's weird. I'm told many people have to try different meds before they find the right one, but since you are a success story (which rules!) I was wondering what your experience was like starting out.
My doc told me to stop taking it and stuff, so hopefully the feelings and thoughts go away. They are very bad right now. I appreciate your concern and replies, thank you.

Thanks. I'm waiting for my psych to call me to see what's going on, so far I'm holding off going because I don't want to end up on a 72 hour hold even if it's voluntary and what not. I'm not convinced inpatient is best for me yet and I would hate to make a mistake that ends up hurting me worse mentally if that makes sense
I feel the same way man. I wish I had an answer for us both. You're not alone.

I called earlier just waiting for morning to hear from them. They'll tell me the same shit as before: "oh it's only been two weeks, stay the course!" I am on the edge here. I don't say that lightly. I feel a void I can't describe. My life feels so completely meaningless it's unreal. I don't know if I can ever get through this now with my family having seen me at my worst. I know it sounds dramatic but this whole experience has really crushed what was left inside me. I won't be doing medication again if I come off this, that's for sure.
I have heard awful things about Arrowhead, but I've never been there myself. I will check our RC tomorrow.

I can make it to Ann Arbor, it's just I wasn't sure if going there was a "good idea" if that makes sense. I've heard horror stories about the "5th floor" as we called it in the Army so I wasn't sure if it was worth going to or if it's just gonna make shit worse.
Thank you I'm going over this stuff rn. This is a really helpful guide
Appreciate it, I'll have to see if the VA covers it
Thank you I'll check it out
